_comment: A connector is DATA, never code. It says how to read a file, never WHERE that file is - the human picks it. Paths use dots for object keys and [] to walk an array. Nothing here is evaluated.
_verified: NOT MEASURED. Written on 2026-09-11 against the documented shape of the claude.ai export; no real export existed on this machine to run it over. Everything below is a BELIEF about the format. The fixture proves the reader, not the mapping.
_where: Settings > Privacy > Export data. Anthropic mails a link; the zip holds conversations.json, projects.json and users.json.
_noBranches: Unlike the OpenAI export, this one carries an ordered message list with no regeneration siblings, so nothing is abandoned and abandonedTurns stays 0. That is a fact about the format, not a better reader.

archive._textWhy: 'text' is read first and 'content' only when it is empty. Older exports carry the whole turn in 'text'; newer ones carry typed content parts and leave 'text' as a flattened copy. Preferring 'text' keeps both readable, and the parts walk is what catches an attachment-only turn.
archive._rolesWhy: This export says 'human', not 'user'. Guessing between the two spellings is how a reader silently files the model's words as the person's, which is why roles are declared rather than inferred.

_mark: DRAWN, not traced: no Anthropic asset ships on this machine to vectorise, so this is the same rendering of the Claude burst the claude-code connector carries, and this field says plainly that it is an approximation. Tony authorised approximate marks on 2026-09-06 after the risk was named. The day an official path exists it replaces this one, with no code change.
